extracted.intended_audience: painters, art students, and apprentices seeking practical guidance on painting
extracted.subtask_description: General instructional guidance and evaluative criteria for practicing, studying, and judging painting (studio methods, perspective, anatomy, composition, gesture, memory, and professional conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express the original idea in drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: “First strive in drawing to express to the eye in a manifest shape the idea and the fancy originally devised by thy imagination.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin by making the idea visible in drawing, then iteratively add or remove elements until satisfied; arrange models (clothed or nude) to suit the intention of the work. Avoid letting the lust of gain overcome the honour of thy art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony with perspective and natural effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that “as regards dimension and size, in accordance with perspective there is no portion of the work which is not in harmony with reason and natural effects.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that every portion of the picture obeys correct proportions and perspective relationships so that scale, distance and size feel natural and reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render light, shade, colour, aerial perspective and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting should represent the colours of all objects and their gradations; it can show transparent bodies, reflections, mists, dark skies and infinite effects which sculpture cannot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop techniques to depict light and shade, colour gradations, atmospheric (aerial) perspective, reflections and translucency to convey depth, distance and material qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build work on the solid foundations of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: “Unless thou build it on the solid foundations of nature, thou shalt reap but scant honour and gain by thy work.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base studies and compositions on careful observation of natural forms rather than on formulaic or purely decorative conventions to achieve lasting honour and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain knowledge first, then practice
rubrics_metrics.description: “Knowledge is the captain, and practice the soldiers.” Practice should always be based on sound theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize learning (theory, observation, principles) before or alongside repetitive practice so that technique is guided by understanding rather than blind repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master perspective and related mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: “Perspective must therefore be placed at the head of all human study and discipline...in it resides the glory of physics as well as of mathematics.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn the principles and demonstrations of perspective and the necessary mathematics as foundational tools for convincing representation of space and light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn anatomy: limbs, actions, then composition
rubrics_metrics.description: “The first thing which should be learnt is the mechanism of the limbs, and when this knowledge has been acquired their actions should come next, and thirdly the composition of subjects.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the structure of the body first (bones, muscles), then how bodies act under circumstances, then use that knowledge to compose full scenes; use simple gesture marks (O for head, lines for limbs) for quick studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer copying from nature (and select good masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy from some good master to accustom thyself to well-drawn forms, then from nature to acquire confirmation of the theories...it is safer to go to nature than to what to its deterioration is imitated from nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use masterworks as models only when they are well composed; always return to direct observation of nature to avoid bad habits learned from poor imitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a portable coloured-paper notebook of sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry a little note-book of coloured paper; what you write may not be rubbed out...these things should not be rubbed out, but preserved with great care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make brief marks in the field (gesture, circumstance, poses) and preserve them as a personal archive of observations to be worked up later; do not erase but replace used books to keep a continuous record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rules to correct figures, not to compose
rubrics_metrics.description: These rules are only to be used in correcting the figures...But if thou attemptest to apply these rules in composition thou wilt never finish anything, and confusion will enter into thy work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply measurement rules and corrective principles to refine, not to dictate initial creative composition—overreliance will hinder completion and invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constantly check measurements; do not trust the eye alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists do not trust to the judgement of the eye...they proceed by continually checking the height, thickness and breadth of each part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt measuring practices and repeated checks rather than relying solely on subjective visual judgment, because the eye is deceptive in exact proportioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a mirror to compare picture and reality
rubrics_metrics.description: When thou wishest to see whether thy picture corresponds entirely with the objects thou hast drawn from nature, take a mirror...and compare the reflection with thy picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the painted image with the flat mirror reflection of the living subject—the mirror is a practical master for assessing whether outlines, lights and shadows produce the same relief and distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate solitude and focused observation
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter should be solitary, and take note of what he sees and reason with himself...solitude helps the mind to concentrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize distracting company while studying; solitude aids deep observation and reflection necessary for accurate memory and invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the mind like a mirror: imprint and classify observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The mind of the painter must be like unto a mirror, which ever takes the colour of the object it reflects...imprint them in his memory and classify them and deduce rules from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train memory to retain many image-forms, classify recurring patterns, and extract practical rules from observed phenomena for future invention and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mottled walls/clouds (pareidolia) as invention aids
rubrics_metrics.description: When you look at walls mottled with various stains...you may discover...the likeness of various countries, adorned with mountains, rivers...battles and figures in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use random patterns as prompts for imaginative invention—translate accidental shapes into harmonious compositions and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study practical anatomy (dissection if possible) for precision
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain true and complete knowledge of these veins I have destroyed more than ten human bodies...until I finished by acquiring perfect knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible and tolerable, study real anatomy deeply (including dissection) to learn fine structural details; acknowledge practical and moral constraints and the need for drawing mastery to record findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice mental rehearsal to fix outlines in memory
rubrics_metrics.description: It is useful when you are in bed in the dark to work with the imagination, summing up the external outlines of the forms previously studied...this is a laudable practice and useful in impressing objects on the memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quiet periods and imagination to rehearse and consolidate observed forms so they remain available for creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept and weigh criticism; amend when justified
rubrics_metrics.description: While a man is painting he should not be loth to hear every opinion...consider and reflect well whether he who blames has good ground or not to blame thee, and if thou thinkest that he has, amend thy work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listen patiently to critiques (even from non-painters who can judge forms), evaluate the merit of the criticism, and change the work when criticism is well-founded; defend your choices by reason when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer works at different price levels
rubrics_metrics.description: They...declare that they will not give good work for poor payment...Cannot such men reserve some good work and say, 'This is costly; this is moderate, and this is cheap work,' and show that they have work at every price?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a range of quality/price options instead of refusing lower-paid commissions outright—reserve some works for higher remuneration but demonstrate versatility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repeating the same themes, types, faces or movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Radically wrong is the procedure of some masters...repeating the same themes...their types of beauty are likewise the same...in nature they are never repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek variety in subjects, physiognomy and gestures; avoid recycling familiar motifs and prevent your figures from all resembling one another or yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict gestures that reveal the mind’s purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: You must depict your figures with gestures which will show what the figure has in his mind...The most admirable figure is that which best expresses the passion of its mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose poses and movements so that they communicate inner feelings and intentions; study expressive gesture (and learn from mute persons who excel in gesture) to make thought visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reproducing the artist’s own physical defects
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter should portray his figure according to the measurements of a natural body...measure himself and see in which part his own figure varies...and try his utmost to avoid the defects which exist in his own person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-assess and correct your tendencies to reproduce your own proportions or deformities in your work; deliberate study and practice are required to counteract these biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe how age and circumstance change movements
rubrics_metrics.description: The movements of men are as varied as the circumstances which pass through their minds; in the same circumstance an old man or a youth will make a different movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account the age, strength and situational context of figures when posing and depicting motion—gestural nuance should reflect personal and circumstantial differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use perspective, measurements and architecture when judging pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first place thy perspective be sound, then acquire a complete knowledge of the measurements of man and other animals, and of good architecture...and in cases where thou hast no experience do not refuse to draw them from nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating pictures, check for correct perspective, anatomical measurement and believable architectural forms; draw from nature where experience is lacking to inform judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a clean, comfortable, mentally conducive studio
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter with great leisure sits before his work well clothed...his dwelling is full of beautiful pictures, and it is clean; sometimes he has music or readers of diverse and pleasant works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the studio environment supports intellectual work—cleanliness, comfort, leisure and pleasant distractions (music, reading) help the painter’s mental exertion; small rooms aid concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep an artistic ideal and humility; do not let avarice obstruct progress
rubrics_metrics.description: When the work exceeds the ideal of the artist, the artist makes scant progress; and when the work falls short of his ideal it never ceases to improve, unless avarice be an obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold an aspirational standard for work and retain humility—profit motives should not replace the pursuit of the artist’s ideal, which drives continual improvement.
